use_cases.title: AI-assisted generation of first-draft executive and detailed variance commentary from the validated dataset, using approved prompts/templates that explain drivers (price, volume, mix, FX, timing, one-off) and flag items requiring business confirmation.
use_cases.justification: The automation score of 68/100 and 422 analyst hours freed (~0.2 FTE, ~60% drafting reduction) signal genuine value, but the 44.1-month payback against a $101,000 implementation cost and only $27,456 annual savings breaches typical 24-month ROI thresholds — proceeding requires cost reduction or scope expansion to strengthen the economics.
key_requirements: Excel/CSV or dataset connector for validated variance data

risks.risk: Hallucinated or fabricated driver attribution (e.g., inventing an FX or one-off explanation not supported by the validated dataset) misleading management reporting
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict grounding to the validated dataset, mandatory 'driver requires confirmation' flagging, retrieval-constrained prompts, and human FP&A review gate before any commentary is published

risks.risk: Payback of 44.1 months causes the initiative to be defunded or deprioritized mid-implementation, stranding the $101K investment
risks.mitigation: Phase delivery so a minimal executive-summary template ships first to bank early hours saved; expand scope to more entities/cycles to improve the ROI trajectory before full build-out

risks.risk: Nuanced driver misclassification (price vs. volume vs. mix vs. timing) producing plausible but incorrect narrative that erodes stakeholder trust
risks.mitigation: Structured driver decomposition upstream of the LLM (rules compute the numbers, LLM only narrates), plus confidence flagging and a calibration period comparing AI drafts to analyst-authored commentary

risks.risk: Audit/version-retention and governance overhead exceeds estimate, further inflating the already high $101K cost
risks.mitigation: Leverage existing document management/audit infrastructure rather than building bespoke retention; define retention policy and template versioning standards at design time

use_cases.title: Automate extraction and assembly of actuals, budget, forecast, consolidation and operational driver data from approved sources (HERO/D365, CRAFT/IBM PA, FCCS/GPM/ARCS/TRCS, Fabric Core Data Products, Coupa, Concur, POS) into a standard, dimension-labeled variance dataset each reporting cycle.
use_cases.justification: Despite a strong automation score of 78/100 and 0.55 FTE (~1,134 hours) freed annually, the 33.8-month payback against a $198,000 implementation cost and only $70,308 in annual savings exceeds typical 24-month thresholds, so approval is CONDITIONAL on phasing to accelerate early ROI and de-risk the 8/10 technical complexity.

risks.risk: Source-system heterogeneity (8+ systems with distinct authentication, data models, extraction methods) causes brittle RPA connectors that break on UI/API changes, inflating maintenance cost and eroding the already-thin $70,308 annual savings
risks.mitigation: Prioritize API/data-layer integration (Fabric Core Data Products) over screen-scraping RPA where possible; build modular, per-source adapters with automated health-checks and alerting; reserve RPA only for systems lacking programmatic access

risks.risk: Legacy extract blending (AX V6/regional ERP) into Fabric without approved mapping corrupts the consolidated variance dataset and breaches the stated prohibition
risks.mitigation: Hard conditional routing that quarantines all legacy extracts until approved mapping is applied; block-by-default gate enforced in the pipeline with governance sign-off audit trail

risks.risk: Incomplete or inconsistent mandatory metadata (currency basis, scenario, version, consolidation scope) leads to unauditable variance commentary and rejected close/consolidation cycles
risks.mitigation: Enforce schema-level mandatory-field validation with reject-and-flag logic; reconciliation checks against period/entity/hierarchy alignment before dataset publication

risks.risk: Payback of 33.8 months exposes the initiative to cancellation risk if source systems are re-platformed or the ROI is re-scrutinized mid-implementation
risks.mitigation: Phase delivery to bank incremental savings early; establish stage-gate reviews tied to realized freed-hours KPIs before committing full $198K

use_cases.title: Automate the pre-AI data validation and reconciliation gate — reconcile actuals to management P&L, budget/forecast to EPM version, prior year to published reporting, verify dimension mapping, missing entities/accounts, currency consistency and sign checks — producing a pass/fail reconciliation record.
use_cases.justification: Despite a strong automation score of 76/100 and a solid 73% efficiency gain (~594 hours / 0.29 FTE freed), the 45.9-month payback on a $141K build against only $36,828 in annual savings fails standard FP&A investment thresholds; proceed only if scope is narrowed or the SOX/AI-gating strategic value is explicitly credited beyond direct labor savings.
key_requirements: SQL (querying GL, EPM, and reporting data stores)

risks.risk: Heterogeneous source systems (management P&L, EPM version, prior-year published reporting, GL/subledgers) change format or API, breaking brittle RPA integrations
risks.mitigation: Build API/DB connectors where available instead of screen-scraping, version-lock source layouts, and implement schema-change detection that fails gracefully to manual review

risks.risk: Edge cases (intercompany eliminations, post-close manual journals, currency translation consistency) produce false pass/fail results that erode analyst trust in the gate
risks.mitigation: Maintain a documented exception library, keep tolerance thresholds configurable, and preserve mandatory analyst confirmation with Manager-approved exceptions per SOX segregation of duties

risks.risk: Cost overrun pushes the already-marginal 45.9-month payback beyond viability
risks.mitigation: Phase the build starting with the 3-4 highest-volume checks, gate further spend on demonstrated cycle-time reduction, and reuse existing RPA orchestration infrastructure

risks.risk: Automation is treated as replacing sign-off, weakening SOX controls
risks.mitigation: Explicitly design the bot to produce a pass/fail record that requires human confirmation; never auto-approve exceptions; log all bot actions for audit

use_cases.title: Auto-calculate variance amounts, percentages, favorable/unfavorable indicators (revenue/expense/margin/working-capital logic) and group accounts into standard reporting lines with commentary owner assignment.
use_cases.justification: The automation score of 88/100 and Low complexity (3/10) strongly favor proceeding, but the 34.5-month payback against $20,160 annual savings and $58,000 implementation cost exceeds a typical 18-24 month threshold, so a GO is conditioned on cost reduction or scope expansion.
key_requirements: Configuration-driven mapping tables (CSV/YAML) for reporting-line and owner assignment

risks.risk: Extended payback (34.5 months) means the initiative may not recoup the $58,000 cost before tooling/process changes obsolete it, especially at only 0.14 FTE freed
risks.mitigation: Amortize the $58K across multiple reporting packs by designing the account-mapping and commentary-owner lookups as shared configuration; renegotiate build scope to reuse existing BI/FP&A infrastructure

risks.risk: Edge-case handling for zero/immaterial denominators produces misleading variance percentages that erode analyst trust in the automated output
risks.mitigation: Implement explicit materiality thresholds and suppression rules (e.g., report absolute variance and flag 'N/M' when denominator below threshold); validate against 2-3 historical close cycles before go-live

risks.risk: Account-to-reporting-line and commentary-owner mappings drift as the chart of accounts or org structure changes, causing silent misclassification
risks.mitigation: Establish a governed change-control process for the lookup tables with quarterly review ownership assigned to FP&A; add reconciliation checks that flag unmapped accounts

risks.risk: Favorable/unfavorable sign-convention logic is misapplied across revenue vs. expense vs. margin vs. working-capital account types, inverting the directional interpretation
risks.mitigation: Encode sign conventions in a reviewable rules table tied to account type; run a parallel-run validation where automated F/U flags are reconciled against analyst-prepared output for one full cycle

use_cases.title: Automated materiality screening that applies approved thresholds by reporting level, flags items above threshold plus mandatory-comment triggers (boutique openings, regulatory/legal/tax exposure), and prioritizes items by financial impact and management relevance.
use_cases.justification: With an automation score of 82/100, Low technical complexity (3/10), and $52,080 in annual savings against a $72,000 build, the deterministic, rule-driven nature of materiality screening makes this a straightforward GO despite a 16.6-month payback that sits just beyond the ideal 12-month threshold.

risks.risk: Stale or unmaintained approved threshold tables — if materiality thresholds by reporting level drift from current policy, the automation silently mis-screens items (false negatives suppressing material variances)
risks.mitigation: Establish a governed threshold-table change-control process with versioning, quarterly review sign-off by FP&A leadership, and audit logging of every threshold change

risks.risk: Qualitative trigger gaps — keyword-based detection of boutique openings, regulatory/legal/tax exposures may miss items expressed in non-standard language, causing mandatory-comment items to slip through
risks.mitigation: Maintain a curated, expandable trigger dictionary; add a periodic sampling audit of unflagged items and a feedback loop where analysts tag missed triggers to refine the keyword set

risks.risk: Data quality / GL mapping inconsistency — variance tables with misclassified accounts or reporting-level errors feed incorrect inputs into the screening logic
risks.mitigation: Add input validation and reconciliation checks against the source GL prior to screening, with exception reporting for unmapped or ambiguous line items

risks.risk: Payback exceeds one close-cycle-year (16.6 months) — benefits realization slips if adoption lags or analysts continue parallel manual screening
risks.mitigation: Enforce a hard cutover after a defined parallel-run period; track adoption and manual-effort reduction as gating KPIs to ensure the 80% reduction is actually captured

use_cases.title: AI-driven classification of each material variance into the standard taxonomy (volume, price, mix, FX, timing, recurring, one-off, headcount, campaign phasing, boutique activity, inventory, unknown) with an explained high/medium/low confidence level.
use_cases.justification: The use case earns a solid automation score of 66/100 with meaningful efficiency gains (0.27 FTE / 558 hours freed, ~69% reduction in per-variance effort), but the 41.8-month payback against a $107,000 implementation cost and only $30,690 annual savings is too long to justify unconditional approval; the value is strategic (close-cycle speed and consistency) rather than pure cost recovery.
key_requirements: Vector store / RAG for taxonomy and policy grounding

risks.risk: Misclassification of material variances (e.g., labeling a one-off as recurring, or FX as price) feeding into external/board-facing close commentary
risks.mitigation: Enforce Human-in-Loop sign-off on all high-materiality variances; route all low-confidence classifications to mandatory analyst review; log rationale for audit trail

risks.risk: Payback of 41.8 months exceeds the useful life of the model/taxonomy before cost recovery, given FP&A taxonomy and driver definitions evolve
risks.mitigation: Reduce build cost via reusable infrastructure and phase investment; tie continuation to pilot-validated savings before full spend

risks.risk: Confidence-level calibration is poorly explained or inconsistent, eroding analyst trust and negating the ~69% effort reduction as reviewers re-check everything
risks.mitigation: Require explicit, structured confidence justification tied to data completeness; run calibration validation during pilot; measure analyst override rate as a trust KPI

risks.risk: Input data quality — incomplete or unstructured variance context — degrades classification accuracy, especially for 'mix', 'phasing', and 'boutique activity' categories
risks.mitigation: Establish data-readiness checks and standardized variance data feeds before go-live; default ambiguous cases to 'unknown' with low confidence rather than forcing a category

use_cases.title: Automated capture and archival of execution evidence — prompt/workflow version identifier, input dataset version, execution date and user, source system metadata — attached to the draft in the controlled Microsoft 365 repository.
use_cases.justification: Despite a strong automation score of 84/100 and low technical complexity (3/10), the 24.3-month payback against $48,000 implementation cost and modest $23,660 annual savings sits at the margin of viability, warranting a GO only if scope-bundling or cost-reduction conditions are met.

risks.risk: Metadata source fragmentation — prompt/workflow version, dataset version, and source system metadata originate from multiple systems that may expose inconsistent or incomplete APIs, causing incomplete evidence records
risks.mitigation: Conduct a metadata source inventory during discovery; define a mandatory-field schema and fail-loud validation that flags any run missing required evidence rather than silently archiving partial records

risks.risk: M365 repository write-back errors or incorrect file/version association, leaving evidence attached to the wrong draft — undermining audit integrity
risks.mitigation: Implement transactional write-back with a unique run-ID correlation key linking evidence to the specific draft version; add post-write verification read-back and reconciliation logging

risks.risk: Payback erosion — if run volume or per-run manual effort is lower than assumed, the 24.3-month payback extends further, tipping the case to NO-GO
risks.mitigation: Validate actual run frequency and current manual capture time during a 30-day baseline before committing full build budget; gate spend on confirmed volume

risks.risk: Upstream schema/version drift — changes to the AI workflow's versioning scheme or M365 library structure break the bot, incurring maintenance that further degrades the marginal ROI
risks.mitigation: Externalize field mappings and repository paths into configuration; establish a change-notification link with the platform team owning the AI workflow and M365 governance

use_cases.title: AI quality-review agent that challenges AI-generated commentary — detecting incorrect favorable/unfavorable interpretation, unsupported claims, vague wording, missing drivers/actions and open questions — and outputs a revised version preserving all numbers.
use_cases.justification: With a strong automation score of 76/100 and modest technical complexity (5/10), the use case is fundamentally viable, but the 20.4-month payback against $95,000 implementation cost and only $55,814 annual savings pushes ROI past the typical 12-18 month comfort threshold, warranting conditions before committing capital.
key_requirements: Prompt template / structured output validation (e.g., JSON schema, Pydantic)

risks.risk: Incorrect favorable/unfavorable interpretation — the QA agent itself misjudges variance directionality and 'corrects' commentary that was actually right, propagating errors into senior management reporting
risks.mitigation: Encode explicit account-level sign conventions (revenue vs. cost vs. contra accounts) into the prompt/context; require the agent to output its interpretation logic for each flagged item; maintain human review gate during the first 2-3 cycles

risks.risk: Number alteration — LLM inadvertently changes, rounds, or transposes a figure while revising narrative, violating the verbatim-preservation requirement
risks.mitigation: Deterministic post-processing diff that extracts all numeric tokens from input and output and hard-blocks any output where the numeric set differs; treat as a non-negotiable gating check before release

risks.risk: ROI shortfall — actual savings fall below the projected $55,814, pushing the already-marginal 20.4-month payback further out
risks.mitigation: Track realized analyst hours freed per reporting cycle against the 821-hour target; run a 90-day pilot before full rollout to validate the 76% cycle-time reduction assumption

risks.risk: Analyst over-trust or under-trust — reviewers either rubber-stamp agent output or ignore it entirely, negating the efficiency gain
risks.mitigation: Frame agent output as advisory with confidence-flagged items; capture accept/override rates as a KPI to calibrate trust and tune the model

use_cases.title: AI-assisted identification of variances affecting the full-year outlook — separating timing variances from recurring run-rate impacts and outputting a table of item, current-period impact, likely full-year implication, required forecast action, and owner.
use_cases.justification: Despite a moderate automation score of 61/100 and a healthy ~60% cycle-time reduction freeing 378 analyst hours annually, the 53.5-month payback against $118,000 implementation cost and only $26,460 in annual savings fails standard investment hurdles; the medium complexity (6/10) Human-in-Loop design is sound, but the economics only justify proceeding if implementation cost is reduced or scope is expanded to amortize the build.

risks.risk: Misclassification of timing variances as recurring run-rate impacts (or vice versa) leads to erroneous full-year outlook adjustments and misdirected forecast actions
risks.mitigation: Enforce Human-in-Loop sign-off on every classification; add a mandatory 'items requiring confirmation' flag and require analyst validation before the table feeds any forecast decision

risks.risk: Model breaches the explicit prohibition on quantification by inferring or fabricating full-year dollar implications
risks.mitigation: Constrain output schema to qualitative 'likely full-year implication' language; implement a post-generation validator that rejects any numeric magnitude in prohibited fields

risks.risk: Extended 53.5-month payback outlasts tool/platform lifecycle or budget appetite, stranding the $118K investment before break-even
risks.mitigation: Pursue the conditional cost-reduction and scope-expansion paths; stage the build to defer spend until reuse across cycles/entities is confirmed

risks.risk: Analysts distrust or ignore AI-generated commentary, negating the ~60% cycle-time reduction and 378-hour saving
risks.mitigation: Co-design table format with FP&A leads, run a parallel-run validation period, and track override rates to build calibrated trust

use_cases.title: Automated logging of unresolved data, access or interface issues into ServiceNow (with HERO/D365 linkage to Azure DevOps) and referencing the ticket in the reconciliation record.
use_cases.justification: Despite a strong automation score of 78/100, the economics are prohibitive: a 132.1-month (11-year) payback against $96,000 implementation cost and only $8,721 annual savings makes this indefensible, especially given the Medium (6/10) multi-system integration complexity. The ~0.09 FTE gain (194 hours/year) does not justify the capital outlay.

risks.risk: Multi-system integration fragility across ServiceNow, Azure DevOps (HERO/D365), and reconciliation records — API/schema changes in any system break the ticket cross-referencing logic
risks.mitigation: Build against versioned/stable integration endpoints, implement automated regression tests on each system's interface, and establish change-notification agreements with each platform owner

risks.risk: Governance friction — any ServiceNow workflow change must be coordinated with CHANEL TECH and the incumbent ServiceNow provider, inflating both implementation timeline and the already-unfavorable cost base
risks.mitigation: Pre-negotiate a change-request SLA and scope boundary with both parties before committing capital; treat unresolved governance sign-off as a hard gate

risks.risk: Sunk-cost exposure — spending $96,000 to recover only $8,721/year risks stranded investment if the reconciliation process or toolchain is re-platformed before payback (11 years)
risks.mitigation: Do not proceed as a standalone build; defer until it can ride an existing integration program, reducing marginal cost dramatically

risks.risk: Incorrect ticket linkage writing bad references into reconciliation records, creating audit/traceability defects in an FP&A control environment
risks.mitigation: Add validation-on-write with rollback, human-review sampling of first N linkages, and a reconciliation-record audit log

use_cases.title: Automated enforcement of the pre-finalization sign-off checklist (numbers match dataset, correct budget/forecast versions, all material variances addressed, no confidential detail beyond audience access, files saved to controlled repository) prior to release.
use_cases.justification: Despite a healthy automation score of 71/100 and a strong control/quality rationale, the 53.5-month payback against a $131,000 implementation cost and only $29,400 annual savings fails standard ROI thresholds; the use case only becomes defensible if scope is narrowed to the deterministic controls or if audit/compliance risk-reduction value is formally credited.
key_requirements: Workflow/BPM engine (e.g., Power Automate, Camunda, or ServiceNow)
SQL (querying source dataset and version metadata)
Document parsing/diff library (numbers extraction, table-vs-narrative comparison)
Rules engine for deterministic validations (version match, repository path enforcement)

risks.risk: Payback of 53.5 months exceeds typical investment horizons; if per-package volume or manual effort is lower than assumed, the $29,400 savings erodes and ROI never materializes
risks.mitigation: Descope to deterministic checks to lower the $131K cost; validate the 2.45 hrs/instance saving with a time-motion study before full build; consider phased release with a stage-gate after the deterministic MVP

risks.risk: Semantic controls (unsupported drivers, appropriateness for management reporting, executive-summary consistency) are automated beyond a rules engine's capability, producing false pass/fail and undermining trust in the gate
risks.mitigation: Keep these as mandatory human sign-off gates with the workflow only routing/enforcing evidence capture; do not attempt full adjudication in Phase 1

risks.risk: Confidentiality-scoping control (no detail beyond audience access) fails silently, leaking sensitive figures to under-authorized recipients
risks.mitigation: Integrate with existing access/entitlement metadata; hard-block release on unresolved audience mismatches; log all overrides for audit

risks.risk: Automated 'numbers-match-dataset' check becomes brittle against evolving source schemas/version conventions, generating false failures that erode adoption
risks.mitigation: Build tolerance thresholds and clear reconciliation exception reporting; version the mapping layer; monitor false-positive rate as a KPI

use_cases.title: Automated escalation triggers that notify FP&A Manager/Finance Director and Information Security when defined conditions occur — repeated AI numerical errors, actuals materially differing from forecast, significant full-year risk, or suspected data mishandling.
use_cases.justification: Despite a solid automation score of 74/100 and meaningful risk-mitigation value, the 35.0-month payback against $36,000 annual savings versus $105,000 implementation cost is too long for an unconditional GO; proceed only if scope is narrowed to reduce cost and the compliance/reputational protection value is formally recognized as a non-financial justification.

risks.risk: False positives from fuzzy thresholds ('materially differ', 'repeated errors') flood the Finance Director and InfoSec with unwarranted escalations, eroding trust in the system
risks.mitigation: Calibrate thresholds against 6-12 months of historical variance data, implement a tunable sensitivity buffer, and run a parallel shadow-mode period before live escalation routing

risks.risk: Missed escalation (false negative) — a genuine material variance or data-mishandling event fails to trigger, creating compliance and reputational exposure
risks.mitigation: Build a periodic reconciliation audit that cross-checks bot detections against manual sampling, plus a heartbeat/failure alert if the bot stops processing

risks.risk: Integration fragility across multiple systems (FP&A data sources, email/notification, InfoSec incident management) causes bot breakage after upstream schema or UI changes
risks.mitigation: Prefer API-based connectors over screen-scraping where available, add exception handling with fallback manual alerting, and establish a maintenance SLA

risks.risk: Extended 35.0-month payback exposes the initiative to budget cancellation or scope creep before break-even is realized
risks.mitigation: Phase delivery to capture the highest-value trigger (material variance) first, demonstrating early value; document risk-avoidance benefits to justify continued funding

use_cases.title: AI-assisted rewriting of draft commentary to improve clarity, precision and executive readability while preserving exact numbers and financial facts, and making commentary action-oriented in Chanel's discreet tone.
use_cases.justification: Despite a solid automation score of 68/100 and a technically favorable Medium complexity (5/10), the 118.6-month payback against a $97,000 implementation cost and only $9,818 in annual savings makes an unconditional GO financially indefensible; proceeding is only justified if implementation cost is materially reduced or the scope is expanded across more FP&A commentary volume.
